For the parametric curve (shown above)

$$
x=\frac{7}{2}\left({t}^{4}+t-1\right),\,y=\frac{1}{2}\left({t}^{3}\right),\,-\infty <t<\infty ,
$$

 find the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=\frac{7}{2}\left(4{t}^{3}+1\right),\,{y}^{′}(t)=\frac{1}{2}\left(3{t}^{2}\right).
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(3{t}^{2}\right)}{\frac{7}{2}\left(4{t}^{3}+1\right)}.
$$

At the point where $t=-1$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(3(-1)^{2}\right)}{\frac{7}{2}\left(4(-1)^{3}+1\right)} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(3\right)}{\frac{7}{2}\left((-4)+1\right)} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\left(-1\right)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

derivative_domain.condition: x'(t) and y'(t) exist and x'(t) != 0
